# The CJW Themes Jumper extension

`cjw_multisite` is a site package built around one theme extension: **CJW Themes Jumper** (`cjw_themes_jumper`). The
extension draws the site; the packages only bring the content and the install scripts. This page describes what the
extension contains, how the installer wires it in, and what to know when you set it up yourself. It is for designers
who want to see a theme extension that a site package depends on, and for administrators who need to know why the
extension must be in place before installing.

## The extension in short

| Fact | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Name | CJW Themes Jumper | `ezinfo.php`, `extension.xml` |
| Version in Exponential 6.0.15 | 0.1.6 | `ezinfo.php` `Version`; the root `composer.json` requires `se7enxweb/cjw_themes_jumper` `~0.1.6` |
| Copyright | 2007 - 2026 CJW Network, JAC Systeme GmbH and 7x | `ezinfo.php` |
| License | GNU General Public License v2.0 (or any later version) | `ezinfo.php`, `composer.json` (`GPL-2.0-or-later`) |
| Repository | [se7enxweb/cjw_themes_jumper](https://github.com/se7enxweb/cjw_themes_jumper) | `Info_url` |
| Composer type | `ezpublish-legacy-extension` | `composer.json` |

Its README calls it "The design `starter` for Exponential 6: the look of the Nexus v2 CJW starter site, ported to
plain Exponential template code." The first release, 0.1.0, is described in its `CHANGELOG.md` as "a port of the
Nexus v2 CJW starter look to Exponential 6"; later releases added Open Graph tags (0.1.2), a register link only for
visitors who may register (0.1.3), an escaping fix in the map popup (0.1.4) and contrast and target size fixes
(0.1.5).

## What it brings

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| The design `starter`: page layout, header, offcanvas menu, breadcrumb, pre-footer, footer; full, line, list, tile, teaser, slide, gallery and embed views of the starter classes; search, sign-in, registration, password and error pages; feedback forms with a honeypot field | `design/starter/` |
| Templates for the layout blocks of the starter layouts, including paged list and grid blocks | `design/starter/`, module `cjw_paging` |
| The custom XML tags of the starter content, with plain renderings for every other design | `design/standard/templates/`, `settings/content.ini.append.php` |
| The image aliases `cjw_i30` ... `cjw_i1920` and 16:9 crops, drawn by `cjwJumperImagineImageHandler` | `settings/image.ini.append.php`, `classes/` |
| Cached map tiles for the Leaflet maps | module `osm_proxy`, `settings/osm_proxy.ini.append.php` |
| German design strings | `translations/ger-DE/` |
| **The images and files of the starter content** | `share/content-images/` (74 files in 6.0.15), `share/content-files/` (3 files) |

The `share/` folders are the reason the content package is small: `cjw_multisite_democontent` names each file with an
`extension-path` into these folders instead of carrying it (see
[The demo content package](the-demo-content-package.md#simple-files-that-point-into-the-extension)).

## Global and siteaccess settings

The extension is meant to be a **global** extension (`ActiveExtensions[]`), but only a few things are global:

| Global (`settings/`) | Per siteaccess (`settings/siteaccess/cjw_starter/`) |
|---|---|
| `content.ini.append.php` (custom XML tags), `design.ini.append.php`, `image.ini.append.php`, `cjw_jumper.ini.append.php`, `osm_proxy.ini.append.php` | `site.ini.append.php`, `override.ini.append.php`, `module.ini.append.php`, `collect.ini.append.php`, `explayouts.ini.append.php` |

The global part lets every siteaccess (the admin and the online editor too) open and save starter content without
losing its custom tags. Everything that changes how a site behaves (template overrides, search handling, information
collection, block view types, the modules `osm_proxy` and `cjw_paging`) is in the `cjw_starter` folder and reaches a
siteaccess only through:

```ini
[SiteAccessSettings]
ExtensionSettingsSiteAccess=cjw_starter
```

The design finds what its page chrome needs by remote id, never by node id (`settings/cjw_jumper.ini.append.php`):
for example `[SiteInfo] NodeRemoteID=cjw-starter-n-65` and `[Header] TopLinkContainerNodeRemoteID=cjw-starter-n-1292`.
That is why the same settings work on every installation of the starter content.

## How cjw_multisite uses it

| When | What the installer does | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Extension list | Puts `cjw_themes_jumper` (and `cjw_tmv` when present) in `ActiveExtensions[]`, after the other themes | `initSettings()` |
| Before the packages | Links the 158 simple files from `share/` into the content package | `cjwLinkStarterFilesFromExtension()` |
| User siteaccess | `SiteDesign=starter`, `AdditionalSiteDesignList[]=standard`, `ExtensionSettingsSiteAccess=cjw_starter`; logs "extension/cjw_themes_jumper is not there: the starter design is missing" when the folder is absent | `postInstallUserSiteaccessINIUpdate()` |
| Overrides of other extensions | Override blocks that another active extension ships for a siteaccess of the same name are taken out of use in the siteaccess's own `override.ini.append.php` | `cjwWriteStarterSiteaccessOverrides()` |
| Roles | Anonymous and Member get `osm_proxy/tiles` | `siteRoles()` |
| After the install | Removes the links into `share/` again | `cjwUnlinkStarterFilesFromExtension()` |

The override step exists because `standard` is the starter design's only fallback: an override whose template the
`starter` to `standard` chain does not have would render an empty page. Each such block gets
`Source=cjw/override_not_used_by_the_starter_design.tpl`. The extension's own overrides in `cjw_starter` are not
touched.

> **Warning**
> Keep `share/content-images/` and `share/content-files/` in place on any installation that may install
> `cjw_multisite` again. The extension's INSTALL.md says the same: the content package "reads the images and files
> of that content from" those folders.

## Setting it up by hand

For a siteaccess of your own (not installed by `cjw_multisite`), the extension's `INSTALL.md` gives these steps:

```ini
# settings/override/site.ini.append.php
[ExtensionSettings]
ActiveExtensions[]=cjw_themes_jumper

# settings/siteaccess/<siteaccess>/site.ini.append.php
[SiteAccessSettings]
ExtensionSettingsSiteAccess=cjw_starter

[DesignSettings]
SiteDesign=starter
AdditionalSiteDesignList[]
AdditionalSiteDesignList[]=standard
```

Then give the siteaccess its content root (`[NodeSettings] RootNode`, `IndexPage`, `DefaultPage`), add it to
`AvailableSiteAccessList[]` and `SiteList[]`, and clear the caches:

```bash
php bin/php/ezpgenerateautoloads.php -e
php bin/php/ezcache.php --clear-tag=ini --allow-root-user
php bin/php/ezcache.php --clear-tag=template --allow-root-user
php bin/php/ezcache.php --clear-id=template-override --allow-root-user
```

Without the starter content the design has little to draw: it expects the classes and remote ids of
`cjw_multisite_democontent`.

## Requirements

From the extension's README:

- [ ] Exponential 6 with the `standard` design, PHP 8.0 or later.
- [ ] `explayouts` and `ezjscore` (jQuery) for the pages and blocks.
- [ ] The PHP extension `imagick` for the `cjw_*` image aliases.
- [ ] Optional: `cjw_tmv`, the TMV event feed, for the event container pages. Exponential 6.0.15 requires
  `se7enxweb/cjw_tmv` `~0.1.2` in its root `composer.json`; its account is set per installation in
  `settings/override`, never in a package (the installer's comment).

The map tiles are fetched by `osm_proxy` from the server named in `settings/osm_proxy.ini.append.php`; mind that
server's tile usage policy.
